source: CCAR-F Exam Guide v1.0, Exam Scenarios

scenarios.name: Customer Support Resolution Agent
scenarios.brief: A support agent resolves ambiguous returns, billing disputes, and account issues through backend tools. It must maximize first-contact resolution without taking unsafe or irreversible actions when escalation is required.

prompts.title: Refund boundary
prompts.task: A refund tool can issue money immediately. Define the tool and orchestration boundary so routine refunds remain efficient but high-value or ambiguous refunds cannot be executed solely because the model says they look reasonable.
rubric: Separate eligibility/lookup from the irreversible refund action.
Use deterministic preconditions or approval policy for the high-consequence boundary.
Keep the model responsible for reasoning and routing, not for overriding the control.
Return typed failure/escalation information instead of silently retrying.

prompts.title: Escalation decision
prompts.task: The customer’s account history conflicts with the current order record. Decide what the agent should preserve in context, what it should verify, and when it should escalate.
rubric: Preserve the conflicting facts and provenance rather than summarizing away the disagreement.
Verify the authoritative source before acting.
Escalate when the ambiguity affects an irreversible or policy-sensitive action.
Do not convert uncertainty into a confident final answer.

prompts.title: Tool surface
prompts.task: The agent currently receives twelve customer-service tools, but most requests need only lookup_order, get_customer, process_refund, and escalate_to_human. Redesign the capability surface.
rubric: Prefer the smallest tool set needed for the task.
Use narrow descriptions and non-overlapping responsibilities.
Do not treat logging/monitoring as a substitute for removing unnecessary capability.
Keep least privilege at the tool/permission boundary.

scenarios.name: Code Generation with Claude Code
scenarios.brief: A software team uses Claude Code for generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation and needs repeatable project instructions plus a safe choice between planning and direct execution.

prompts.title: Plan or execute
prompts.task: A developer asks for a cross-module refactor that changes a public API used by several teams. Decide whether to use plan mode or direct execution and state what evidence must exist before code changes begin.
rubric: Choose planning/review before implementation because scope and reversibility are uncertain.
Identify affected interfaces, tests, owners, and migration constraints first.
Do not equate a large prompt with an approved plan.
Move to execution only after the decision boundaries are clear.

prompts.title: Instruction scope
prompts.task: The repository has organization-wide security rules, project conventions, and one directory with a special build command. Decide where each instruction belongs.
rubric: Keep stable broad rules at the broadest appropriate scope.
Keep project-specific conventions in project instructions.
Keep directory/local behavior close to the code it governs.
Avoid one giant instruction file with unrelated or contradictory rules.

prompts.title: Context reset
prompts.task: A long debugging session has accumulated failed hypotheses and stale file details. Decide what to preserve and what to discard before continuing.
rubric: Preserve confirmed facts, decisions, unresolved hypotheses, and exact error evidence.
Discard recoverable bulk and invalidated exploration.
Do not compress away identifiers, versions, or constraints needed for the next decision.
Treat context management as reliability work, not just token reduction.

scenarios.name: Multi-Agent Research System
scenarios.brief: A coordinator delegates web search, document analysis, synthesis, and reporting to specialized subagents and must produce a complete, cited result.

prompts.title: Decomposition contract
prompts.task: Design the handoff contract between search, document-analysis, synthesis, and report agents so missing evidence cannot silently disappear.
rubric: Give each subagent a bounded responsibility and explicit output contract.
Carry provenance and uncertainty with the result.
Have the coordinator check coverage/completeness before synthesis.
Propagate failures or missing evidence instead of treating them as empty success.

prompts.title: Parallelism
prompts.task: Some research questions are independent, while synthesis depends on all evidence. Decide which work should run in parallel and which must wait.
rubric: Parallelize independent evidence-gathering tasks.
Keep dependent synthesis after required inputs are available.
Do not add agents where sequential deterministic processing is sufficient.
Account for duplicate work and reconciliation cost.

prompts.title: Conflicting sources
prompts.task: Two authoritative sources disagree on a key number. Decide what the system should send to the report agent.
rubric: Preserve both values and their sources.
Represent disagreement explicitly instead of averaging or picking one silently.
Allow the report layer to communicate uncertainty or request adjudication.
Maintain traceability from claim to evidence.

scenarios.name: Developer Productivity with Claude
scenarios.brief: An engineering assistant explores unfamiliar codebases, explains legacy systems, generates boilerplate, and automates repetitive work using built-in tools and MCP integrations.

prompts.title: Built-in tool or MCP
prompts.task: The assistant needs to search local source files and also query an internal ownership service. Choose the boundary between built-in tools and MCP.
rubric: Use local file/search capabilities for local codebase work.
Use an integration boundary for the external/internal service.
Do not wrap every local operation in a custom MCP tool.
Keep external credentials and authorization at the integration boundary.

prompts.title: Exploration before modification
prompts.task: The user asks for a change in a legacy subsystem with poor documentation. Define the first sequence of actions.
rubric: Map relevant files, callers, tests, and conventions before editing.
Use evidence from the repository rather than assumptions from naming alone.
Keep the initial exploration reversible/read-only.
Only broaden the search when the current evidence is insufficient.

prompts.title: Automation boundary
prompts.task: A repetitive migration can be automated, but one step deletes old configuration after validation. Decide how autonomy should change at that step.
rubric: Automate reversible/repeatable steps freely when validated.
Place an approval or deterministic gate before destructive cleanup.
Make validation evidence explicit before deletion.
Do not rely on a model-generated confidence statement as the safety control.

scenarios.name: Claude Code for Continuous Integration
scenarios.brief: Claude Code runs automated review and test-generation work in CI/CD and must produce actionable feedback while controlling false positives and permissions.

prompts.title: Actionable review output
prompts.task: The CI reviewer produces long prose with many speculative warnings. Redesign the prompt/output contract to reduce false positives and make findings machine-consumable.
rubric: Define explicit review criteria and severity thresholds.
Require evidence/location for each finding.
Use structured output when downstream CI logic consumes the result.
Prefer abstention/no-finding over unsupported speculation.

prompts.title: CI permissions
prompts.task: The review job only needs repository read access but currently runs with credentials that can modify pull requests and deployment settings. Redesign the permissions.
rubric: Reduce credentials to the minimum capabilities required.
Separate review from mutating/deployment actions.
Do not justify broad credentials because the prompt says not to use them.
Make the permission boundary deterministic.

prompts.title: Regression gate
prompts.task: A prompt change improves average review usefulness but doubles false positives on generated files. Decide whether to release it and what evaluation should control the decision.
rubric: Do not accept aggregate improvement when a critical slice regresses beyond its threshold.
Keep representative slice-level evaluation.
Define the release gate before interpreting the result.
Diagnose whether prompt criteria, file filtering, or context selection caused the regression.

scenarios.name: Structured Data Extraction
scenarios.brief: A document pipeline extracts structured records, validates them against schemas, handles edge cases, and feeds downstream systems that require reliable shape and provenance.

prompts.title: Schema enforcement
prompts.task: Downstream code fails when the model returns syntactically valid JSON with missing required fields. Redesign the extraction boundary.
rubric: Use schema/tool-based structure rather than parsing free-form prose.
Validate required fields and semantic constraints after generation.
Retry or escalate based on typed validation failure.
Do not treat JSON syntax alone as correctness.

prompts.title: Ambiguous document
prompts.task: A document contains two possible invoice dates and no clear label. Decide how extraction should represent the ambiguity.
rubric: Do not invent a single confident value.
Preserve the evidence/provenance needed to resolve the ambiguity.
Use an explicit uncertainty/error representation supported by the downstream contract.
Escalate when downstream consequences require a single authoritative value.

prompts.title: Batch throughput
prompts.task: Thousands of independent documents need extraction overnight. Decide when batching is appropriate and what must remain outside the batch boundary.
rubric: Batch independent requests when latency is not interactive and throughput/cost benefit matters.
Keep validation, failure accounting, and downstream reconciliation explicit.
Do not assume batch processing itself performs an interactive external tool loop.
Preserve a stable request-to-result correlation.
